profile.reading: TierPoint operates a data center at 820 Allen Commerce Parkway in Allen, Texas, part of the Dallas-Fort Worth metro area in Collin County. TierPoint is a real, established managed IT services and colocation provider headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri, formed in 2010 when it made its first data center acquisition in the Dallas market, and the company now describes its national footprint as roughly 40 data centers across 20 US markets. This Allen facility was announced in 2016 as TierPoint's second Dallas-area data center, a purpose-built new construction rather than an acquisition, backed by an initial investment of more than 20 million dollars and targeted to open in spring 2017, with company chairman and CEO Jerry Kent and then-regional vice president Chris Parsons quoted in the announcement alongside Allen's mayor. TierPoint's current facility page lists the building at more than 29,000 total square feet with more than 16,000 square feet of raised floor, backed by two 2-megawatt and one 1-megawatt redundant generators providing more than 48 hours of runtime, though the original 2016 announcement described a larger roughly 90,000-square-foot building shell, a discrepancy this entry notes honestly rather than resolves, since it most likely reflects a partial build-out of a larger structure rather than an error in either figure. TierPoint markets the site as carrier-neutral with diverse fiber connectivity and a direct DWDM link to the Dallas Infomart carrier hotel, as well as an interconnection link to its original Dallas facility. The building holds SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II certifications (including HITRUST), and is HIPAA, PCI-DSS, GLBA, ISO 27001, and ITAR compliant, though TierPoint does not state a specific Uptime Institute Tier level for this building, only that it is Uptime Institute certified. As is standard industry practice, TierPoint does not publicly disclose its tenants.
profile.research_note: TierPoint is a real, established US managed IT services and colocation company headquartered in St. Louis, MO, formed in 2010 beginning with a Dallas data center acquisition, now operating roughly 40 data centers across 20 US markets. Ownership correction, per this session's research: TierPoint is NOT majority-owned by ABRY Partners as originally assumed. TierPoint's own investor disclosures name a multi-investor structure (TA Associates, Ontario Teachers Pension Plan, Cequel III, RedBird Capital Partners, The Stephens Group, Thompson Street Capital Partners, Jordan/Zalaznick Advisers) with Argo Infrastructure Partners becoming the largest single equity investor in a Feb 2022 $500M investment, and further increasing its ownership stake per a Dec 2025 announcement. The ABRY claim is not asserted anywhere in this project's content. This Allen, TX building was announced in 2016 as TierPoint's second Dallas-area facility, a new-build (not acquisition), with an initial roughly $20M investment targeted to open spring 2017. Current site lists 29,000+ total sqft, 16,000+ raised floor sqft, though the original 2016 announcement described a larger ~90,000 sqft building shell -- a discrepancy noted honestly rather than resolved (likely reflecting a partially built-out shell). Tier certification level (I/II/III/IV) is not disclosed by TierPoint for this building, only general Uptime-Institute-certified and LEED language.

reading.body:
This facility publishes no power capacity or rack count, so its scale relative to AI infrastructure investment cannot be assessed from its operator's spec page. TierPoint operates roughly 40 data centers across 18 to 20 U.S. markets as a colocation and managed services provider, now majority-owned by Argo Infrastructure Partners, which itself became part of Apollo Global Management's infrastructure platform in January 2025. The Dallas-Allen location sits north of the main Dallas market in Collin County.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, of which 18 publish power capacity totaling 468 megawatts. This campus does not appear in that published inventory, placing it outside the ranked set of disclosed capacity in the state. Without a published megawatt figure from the operator, no comparison is possible to other Texas facilities or to AI scaling constraints in the region.

The absence of published specifications for this facility means it does not contribute to the publicly visible baseline of AI-relevant infrastructure capacity in Texas. If the facility hosts significant power and cooling, that capacity is not disclosed in operator marketing materials this site has indexed. Readers tracking grid-constrained AI deployment should note that most of TierPoint's portfolio similarly appears to publish no power specifications.
